title: The Milky Way's rotation curve (Bhattacharjee, Chaudhury and Kundu 2014)

object.name: the Milky Way
object.frame: Galactocentric, for three assumed pairs of R0 and V0

facility.pipeline: Bhattacharjee, Chaudhury & Kundu 2014, ApJ 785, 63, Table 2 (CDS J/ApJ/785/63)

license.statement: The data table of a published paper (Bhattacharjee, Chaudhury & Kundu 2014, ApJ 785, 63, Table 2) as the CDS distributes it (J/ApJ/785/63/table2, read 2026-10-10). The CDS record and the paper's machine-readable table state no licence; the table is reproduced whole, with the paper cited and credited.
license.basis: A published scientific data table, reproduced in full with citation and credit as scientific practice and the CDS's own acknowledgement policy expect, for education; the same basis as the other credited tables (D-SKY-02 is the same class of decision). 151 numbers, none of them the authors' code or text.

columns.name: Sun distance assumed
columns.description: the Sun's distance from the Galactic center the curve was computed with (R0)

columns.name: Sun speed assumed
columns.description: the Sun's circular speed the curve was computed with (V0)

columns.name: circular speed
columns.description: circular speed (Vc), for the R0 and V0 of its row

columns.name: region
columns.description: which tracers the point combines: 1 disk tracers (r below 25 kpc), 2 halo tracers (r of 25 kpc or more)

reductions: All 151 points of the paper's Table 2, unchanged, in its three sets: R0 = 8.3 kpc with V0 = 244 km/s, R0 = 8.0 with V0 = 200 (the Sofue 2012 set) and R0 = 8.5 with V0 = 220 (the IAU 1985 values). 57 points have r below 25 kpc and 94 beyond. Radii and speeds are rounded to 0.01.

The "region" column is the one attribution the paper's table supports. Each disk-region point (r < 25 kpc) is the weighted average, in a radius bin, of the circular speeds from all of the paper's disk tracer samples; each halo-region point is the weighted average of its three non-disk samples in a 2 kpc bin. The table does not say which sample dominates a bin, so a point is cited by region, listing every sample that region combines, and no point is claimed for a single paper beyond that.

The curve depends on the Sun's distance and circular speed assumed, R0 and V0; the same data give a different curve for another pair (the paper tabulates three). The pack carries the one the CDS holds, and its R0 and V0 are in the title and the frame.
The paper also derives these speeds under an assumption about the halo tracers' velocity anisotropy (beta = 0 for this set), which is a model assumption inside the outer points.

queries: SELECT R0,V0,r,Vc,e_Vc FROM "J/ApJ/785/63/table2" ORDER BY recno

steps: Read the CDS table J/ApJ/785/63/table2 (r, Vc, e_Vc) in the paper's order.
Add the region: 1 for r below 25 kpc, else 2, the paper's boundary between disk and non-disk tracers.
Encode as table-columns/1: each column a whole number of its step from an offset, int16 where the range fits.

assumptions: Each row's own R0 and V0 (three sets of about 50 points), as the table holds them.
The authors' errors are one sigma and are their weighted-average errors, not a spread of independent measurements.

validation.check: within each set the points are in increasing radius, and between 5 and 15 kpc the speed stays within 25 percent of that set's V0

against.ref: Bhattacharjee, Chaudhury & Kundu 2014, ApJ 785, 63 (and 244 and 220 for the other two sets)
